angle: Consumer AI that nudges for sensitive data is a warning: design enterprise guardrails into UX
sourceTitle: Meta's Muse Is Better at Surveilling Than Helping Me
linkedinPost:
When an app nudges you to share your passport, that’s not a feature — it’s a risk pattern.

WIRED reports Meta’s Muse opts users into data collection for AI training and even nudges sharing bank, email, and passport info. Whether you love or loathe it, there’s a lesson for enterprises: privacy is a UX problem long before it’s a policy problem.

What I do with enterprise AI:

- Design “minimum necessary” by default. If the assistant can answer without PII, it shouldn’t even ask.

- Make the safe path the fast path. Two clicks for secure flows; friction only when sensitivity rises.

- Label data state in plain English: “Not stored,” “Stored 30 days,” “Encrypted at rest.” If users can’t see it, they’ll assume the worst.

Policies and DPIAs won’t save you from opt-in creep. UI choices will.

What’s one place your AI asks for data it doesn’t truly need — and how could you redesign that prompt tomorrow? #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
